The '''TT-8L/Y7''' was an variant model of the standard [[TT-8L gatekeeper droid/Legends|TT-8L gatekeeper droid]] designed for installation in a door or a door frame.<ref name="NEGTD">''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref> It was nicknamed the "Tattletale" droid.<ref name="BTM">''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]''</ref>

==Description==
The TT-8L/Y7 was designed for direct installation into a door, doorframe, or entrance alcove, the Y7 was a rigid stem constructed of [[Color/Legends|black]] [[Durasteel/Legends|durasteel]]. The [[Photoreceptor/Legends|optical lens]] of the Y7 was capable of scanning in low-light, [[Ultraviolet/Legends|ultraviolet]], and [[Infrared/Legends|infrared]], and illuminating the area with a [[Spotlight/Legends|spotlight]]. It was also protected by a retractable shutter over the eye.<ref name="EGTD" />

The [[Droid/Legends|droid]] had a standard and unremarkable [[intelligence matrix]], but [[Serv-O-Droid, Inc./Legends|Serv-O-Droid]] realized that the limited nature might not appeal to the market they were aiming for with the droid; namely those with a distrustful nature. The Y7s were equipped with a remote-activated subroutine that allowed a [[Security guard/Legends|security guard]] to take control of the droid.<ref name="EGTD" />

==History==
[[File:JabbasTT8L.png|left|thumb|[[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] encounters [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba's]] gatekeeper [[Droid/Legends|droid]].]]
The TT-8L/Y7 model was a variant of the standard [[TT-8L gatekeeper droid/Legends|TT-8L gatekeeper droid]] model. Serv-O-Droid saw that their droid had applications beyond serving the rich; criminals, recluses, and the paranoid also needed a droid that could screen callers. However, in these cases, direct confrontation was a priority and the Y7 model could interrogate visitors and scan them for weapons.<ref name="EGTD" />

Captain [[Neg]] had one TT-8L/Y7 droid guarding the door of his residence in Mos Espa in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]]. While he was hunting [[Bantha/Legends|banthas]] in the [[Dune Sea/Legends|Dune Sea]], [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] tried to enter the house and rescue a local [[Ithorian/Legends|Ithorian]] boy named [[Tomo]]. The droid didn't let the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] enter the house, instead activating the security turrets near the gates, which forced Jinn to enter via a balcony.<ref name="TPM Game">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (video game)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' video game]]</ref>

[[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]] used a sadistic TT-8L/Y7 to guard the gate to his [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|palace]] on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. It let [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] and [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] into the palace in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], who were delivering a message from [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]].<ref name="ROTJ">{{Film|VI}}</ref>

A similar droid guarded [[Ka'Pa's palace]] and didn't allow [[Mara Jade Skywalker|Mara Jade]] audience. Mara had to be disguised as a [[Tusken Raider/Legends|Tusken Raider]] in order to fool the droid.<ref name="Mysteries">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Mysteries of the Sith]]''</ref>

One was part of the entryway security at [[Brogar's Safe House and Cantina]] on [[Lok/Legends|Lok]] in [[137 ABY]], along with a [[Gotal/Legends|Gotal]] [[Unidentified Gotal door attendant|door attendant]].<ref name="Legacy 2">[[Legacy (2006) 2|''Legacy'' (2006) 2]]</ref>
